title: POT GPD MLE VaR and ES at several levels from returns
deliverables: summary json: threshold, n_exceed, xi, beta
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns [n] (decimal); threshold quantile p_u; levels [Q]. DITANYAKAN: u, N_u, xi, beta (scalars); VaR_q, ES_q per level [Q] as positive losses. RUMUS: card Core 1 (L=-r, strict L>u, y=L-u); Core 2 genpareto.fit(y, floc=0) -> (c=xi, 0, beta); Core 3 VaR_q = u + (beta/xi)[((n/N_u)(1-q))^(-xi) - 1], ES_q = VaR_q/(1-xi) + (beta - xi u)/(1-xi). JAWAB: 1) losses [n]. 2) u = empirical quantile p_u of losses (pinned method). 3) excesses y [N_u]. 4) MLE xi, beta. 5) VaR, ES per q. 6) check ES>VaR>u, beta>0, xi<1.
formulas: L = -r; y = L - u for L > u
pitfalls: fitting raw losses instead of excesses
genpareto.fit without floc=0

title: POT threshold from top-k order statistics
deliverables: summary json: k, threshold, xi, beta, var, es
frame: DIKETAHUI: losses [n]; k tail points; level q. DITANYAKAN: u, xi, beta, VaR_q, ES_q. RUMUS: sort descending X_(1)>=...>=X_(n); u = X_(k+1) so exactly k strict exceedances (card V1 a); N_u = k; GPD MLE on y_i = X_(i) - u, i=1..k; Core 3 with N_u/n = k/n. JAWAB: 1) losses = -returns, sort descending. 2) u = X_(k+1). 3) excesses [k]. 4) genpareto.fit(y, floc=0). 5) VaR_q = u + (beta/xi)[((n/k)(1-q))^(-xi)-1]; ES. 6) check q > 1 - k/n so VaR > u.
pitfalls: using X_(k) as u when k excesses are required (gives k-1)

title: POT with X_(k) as threshold (k-1 excesses variant)
deliverables: summary json: threshold, n_exceed, xi, beta
frame: DIKETAHUI: losses [n]; k; text states the k-th largest loss is the threshold. DITANYAKAN: u, N_u, xi, beta, tail quantile. RUMUS: u = X_(k); strict exceedance L > u leaves N_u = k-1 excesses (card V1 b); ties at u excluded; Core 2-3 with N_u = k-1. JAWAB: 1) sort descending. 2) u = X_(k). 3) excesses X_(i) - u, i=1..k-1. 4) MLE (floc=0). 5) VaR/ES with N_u/n = (k-1)/n. 6) report N_u explicitly so the convention is visible.
pitfalls: mixing N_u = k in Core 3 with u = X_(k)

title: Mean excess function table over a threshold grid
frame: DIKETAHUI: losses [n]; threshold grid [G] (quantiles or levels). DITANYAKAN: e(u) per grid point [G], count N_u [G]; chosen u. RUMUS: card Core 4 empirical e(u) = sum_{L>u}(L-u)/N_u; for GPD tail e(u) = (beta + xi u)/(1-xi), linear with slope xi/(1-xi). JAWAB: 1) losses. 2) for each u in grid: strict exceedances, mean excess, N_u. 3) drop points with tiny N_u. 4) choose lowest u above which e(u) is roughly linear (or rule stated). 5) optional: OLS slope s -> xi ~ s/(1+s). 6) write table.
pitfalls: using >= at u (ties) inconsistent with the fit

title: Exponential tail (xi = 0) POT VaR and ES
deliverables: summary json: u, beta, var, es
frame: DIKETAHUI: losses [n]; threshold u; level q; text fixes xi = 0 (exponential excesses). DITANYAKAN: beta, VaR_q, ES_q. RUMUS: card Core 2 xi=0: G(y) = 1 - exp(-y/beta); MLE beta = mean(y); Core 3 xi=0: VaR_q = u - beta ln((n/N_u)(1-q)), ES_q = VaR_q + beta. JAWAB: 1) excesses y [N_u]. 2) beta = mean(y) (or scipy expon.fit(y, floc=0)). 3) VaR, ES per level. 4) check ES - VaR = beta (memoryless).
pitfalls: applying the xi formula with xi -> 0 numerically (division by zero)

title: GPD MLE standard errors from expected information
deliverables: summary json: xi, beta, se_xi, se_beta, ci_xi, ci_beta
frame: DIKETAHUI: excesses [N_u]; confidence c for CI. DITANYAKAN: xi, beta, se and Wald CI. RUMUS: card Core 5 expected info (xi > -0.5): Var(xi) = (1+xi)^2/N_u, Var(beta) = 2 beta^2 (1+xi)/N_u, Cov(xi,beta) = beta(1+xi)/N_u; CI = est +- z_{(1+c)/2} se. JAWAB: 1) MLE (floc=0). 2) plug xi, beta into variances. 3) se = sqrt. 4) Wald CI. 5) check xi > -0.5 else formulas invalid.
pitfalls: using these SEs for xi <= -0.5

title: GPD observed-information SEs via numerical Hessian
deliverables: summary json: xi, beta, cov matrix 2x2, se_xi, se_beta
frame: DIKETAHUI: excesses [N_u]. DITANYAKAN: MLE and covariance from the observed information; optional se of VaR_q by delta method. RUMUS: card Core 5 NLL = N ln beta + (1+1/xi) sum ln(1 + xi y/beta); Cov = inv(Hessian of NLL) = inv(-Hessian of LL). Delta: se(VaR) = sqrt(g' Cov g), g = grad of VaR_q wrt (xi, beta). JAWAB: 1) minimise NLL (multi-start Nelder-Mead, infeasible -> inf). 2) finite-difference Hessian at optimum. 3) invert. 4) se = sqrt(diag). 5) delta method if asked.
formulas: NLL = N ln beta + (1+1/xi) sum ln(1 + xi y/beta)
pitfalls: inverting the LL Hessian without the sign flip (negative variances)

title: Profile likelihood confidence interval for the GPD shape
frame: DIKETAHUI: excesses [N_u]; confidence c. DITANYAKAN: profile-likelihood CI for xi (or for VaR_q via reparametrisation). RUMUS: LL_p(xi) = max_beta LL(xi, beta); CI = {xi: 2[LL_max - LL_p(xi)] <= chi2_{1,c}}. For VaR_q: substitute beta = xi (VaR - u)/[((n/N_u)(1-q))^(-xi) - 1] and profile over VaR. JAWAB: 1) global MLE. 2) grid of xi; inner 1-D maximisation in beta. 3) deviance per grid point. 4) find crossings by brentq. 5) report asymmetric CI.
pitfalls: using a grid too coarse to locate crossings

title: GPD method-of-moments estimates (MLE starting values)
frame: DIKETAHUI: excesses [N_u]. DITANYAKAN: MoM xi, beta (and use as MLE start). RUMUS: card Completing: m = mean(y), v = var(y); xi0 = 0.5(1 - m^2/v), beta0 = 0.5 m (1 + m^2/v); valid for xi < 0.5 (finite variance). JAWAB: 1) m, v (state ddof). 2) xi0, beta0. 3) if MLE asked, start Nelder-Mead from (xi0, beta0) and other starts. 4) report both.
pitfalls: ddof mismatch with a pinned variance definition

title: GPD probability-weighted moments (Hosking-Wallis)
frame: DIKETAHUI: excesses [N_u]. DITANYAKAN: PWM estimates of xi, beta (card V3 b). RUMUS: sort ascending y_(1..N); a0 = mean(y); a1 = (1/N) sum (1 - p_j) y_(j) with p_j = (j - 0.35)/N; in Hosking-Wallis k = -xi parametrisation: xi = 2 - a0/(a0 - 2 a1), beta = 2 a0 a1/(a0 - 2 a1). JAWAB: 1) sort. 2) plotting positions. 3) a0, a1. 4) xi, beta (state sign convention). 5) optionally compare with MLE.
pitfalls: sign of shape: Hosking k = -xi

title: Evaluate GPD negative log-likelihood at given parameters
frame: DIKETAHUI: excesses [N_u]; candidate (xi, beta) or a grid. DITANYAKAN: NLL value(s); feasibility. RUMUS: card Core 5: NLL = N ln beta + (1+1/xi) sum ln(1 + xi y/beta) (xi != 0); xi = 0: N ln beta + sum y/beta; infeasible (inf) if beta <= 0 or any 1 + xi y/beta <= 0. Cross-check: -sum genpareto.logpdf(y, xi, 0, beta). JAWAB: 1) validate support. 2) compute NLL. 3) cross-check with scipy. 4) write value or table.
formulas: NLL = N ln beta + (1 + 1/xi) sum ln(1 + xi y/beta)
xi=0: NLL = N ln beta + sum y/beta
pitfalls: returning NaN instead of inf for infeasible points

title: Threshold stability plot: xi and modified scale across thresholds
deliverables: per-threshold table: u, n_exceed, xi, beta, beta_star
frame: DIKETAHUI: losses [n]; thresholds [G]. DITANYAKAN: xi(u), beta(u), modified scale beta* = beta - xi u per u. RUMUS: if GPD holds above u0, then for u > u0 xi constant and beta(u) = beta(u0) + xi(u - u0), so beta* constant (Coles 2001). JAWAB: 1) for each u: excesses, MLE (floc=0). 2) beta* = beta - xi u. 3) table [G]. 4) choose smallest u beyond which xi and beta* are stable (within CI). 5) write.
pitfalls: refitting with free location

title: POT tail probability of exceeding a given loss
frame: DIKETAHUI: losses [n]; threshold u; loss levels x [M] (x > u). DITANYAKAN: P(L > x) per level; optional return period 1/P in observations. RUMUS: card Core 3 tail: P(L > x) = (N_u/n)(1 + xi (x-u)/beta)^(-1/xi); xi=0: (N_u/n) exp(-(x-u)/beta); for x <= u use empirical. JAWAB: 1) fit xi, beta. 2) evaluate per x. 3) return period = 1/P (days) if asked. 4) check monotone decreasing in x.
pitfalls: applying GPD formula below the threshold

title: POT return level for an m-observation horizon
frame: DIKETAHUI: losses [n] at frequency f per year; return period T years (m = T f observations). DITANYAKAN: level x_m exceeded on average once per m observations. RUMUS: x_m = u + (beta/xi)[(m N_u/n)^xi - 1] (Coles 2001, = VaR at q = 1 - 1/m); xi=0: u + beta ln(m N_u/n). JAWAB: 1) fit POT. 2) m = T x observations per year. 3) x_m. 4) optional CI by delta method. 5) check x_m increasing in T.
formulas: m = T x obs per year
pitfalls: mixing block-maxima return levels with POT return levels

title: Hill estimator of the tail index
deliverables: summary json: k, xi_hill, alpha, se, ci
frame: DIKETAHUI: losses [n] (positive in tail); k. DITANYAKAN: xi_H, alpha = 1/xi_H, se, CI. RUMUS: card Core 6 sort descending; xi_H = (1/k) sum_{i=1..k} ln X_(i) - ln X_(k+1); se = xi_H/sqrt(k); alpha se = alpha/sqrt(k); CI = xi_H +- z se. JAWAB: 1) losses = -returns, sort descending. 2) check X_(k+1) > 0. 3) xi_H. 4) alpha. 5) se, CI. 6) write.
formulas: xi_H = (1/k) sum ln X_(i) - ln X_(k+1)
pitfalls: using k+1 points or X_(k) as reference
log of non-positive order statistics

title: Hill plot over a range of k
deliverables: per-k table: k, xi_hill, alpha, se
frame: DIKETAHUI: losses [n]; k grid [K]. DITANYAKAN: xi_H(k), alpha(k), se(k) per k; chosen k. RUMUS: card Core 6 vectorised: cumulative sums of ln X_(i): xi_H(k) = cumsum(lnX)[k-1]/k - lnX_(k+1). JAWAB: 1) sort descending, logs. 2) cumsum. 3) per k xi_H, alpha, se. 4) choose k in the stable plateau (or stated rule, e.g. k = floor(sqrt(n))). 5) write table.
formulas: xi_H(k) = cumsum(ln X)_k / k - ln X_(k+1)
pitfalls: off-by-one indexing between k and X_(k+1)

title: Weissman extreme quantile from the Hill estimator
frame: DIKETAHUI: losses [n]; k; levels [Q]. DITANYAKAN: VaR_q per level; optional ES. RUMUS: card Core 6 VaR_q = X_(k+1) (k/(n(1-q)))^xi_H; Pareto-tail ES_q = VaR_q/(1 - xi_H) (xi_H < 1). JAWAB: 1) xi_H at k. 2) VaR per q. 3) ES if asked. 4) check VaR_q > X_(k+1) when 1-q < k/n.
pitfalls: exponent sign: (k/(n(1-q)))^(+xi)

title: Pickands estimator of the extreme value index
frame: DIKETAHUI: losses [n]; k with 4k <= n. DITANYAKAN: xi_P (valid for any sign of xi). RUMUS: sorted descending X_(1)>=...: xi_P = (1/ln 2) ln[(X_(k) - X_(2k))/(X_(2k) - X_(4k))]. JAWAB: 1) sort descending. 2) pick X_(k), X_(2k), X_(4k). 3) xi_P. 4) optional table over k. 5) compare with Hill (Hill only for xi > 0).
pitfalls: 1-based vs 0-based index for X_(k)

title: Dekkers-Einmahl-de Haan moment estimator
frame: DIKETAHUI: losses [n] (positive tail); k. DITANYAKAN: xi_M (valid for all xi). RUMUS: M1 = (1/k) sum_{i<=k} (ln X_(i) - ln X_(k+1)) (= Hill); M2 = (1/k) sum (ln X_(i) - ln X_(k+1))^2; xi_M = M1 + 1 - 0.5 (1 - M1^2/M2)^(-1). JAWAB: 1) sort descending, logs. 2) M1, M2. 3) xi_M. 4) report alongside Hill.

title: GEV block maxima MLE
deliverables: summary json: n_blocks, mu, sigma, xi
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns [n] with dates; block size (month/year or b observations). DITANYAKAN: block maxima [B]; GEV mu, sigma, xi. RUMUS: card Core 7 H(x) = exp(-(1 + xi (x-mu)/sigma)^(-1/xi)); scipy genextreme.fit(M) -> (c, loc, scale) with xi = -c (OPPOSITE sign to genpareto). JAWAB: 1) losses = -returns. 2) group by block, take max [B] (drop incomplete blocks if stated). 3) fit. 4) xi = -c. 5) check sigma > 0, xi sign sensible (heavy tail > 0).
pitfalls: sign flip of genextreme c

title: GEV return level for an m-block return period
frame: DIKETAHUI: GEV (mu, sigma, xi) or block maxima [B]; return periods m [P] in blocks. DITANYAKAN: z_m per period. RUMUS: card Core 7 z_m = mu - (sigma/xi)[1 - (-ln(1-1/m))^(-xi)]; xi = 0: z_m = mu - sigma ln(-ln(1-1/m)); equivalently genextreme.ppf(1-1/m, c=-xi, loc, scale). JAWAB: 1) fit if needed. 2) z_m per m. 3) cross-check with ppf. 4) check increasing in m.
pitfalls: passing xi rather than -xi as scipy c

title: Daily VaR implied by a block-maxima GEV fit
frame: DIKETAHUI: GEV fit on maxima of blocks of b daily losses; daily levels [Q]. DITANYAKAN: daily VaR_q. RUMUS: card Core 7 F_daily(x) = H(x)^(1/b) -> VaR_q solves H(x) = q^b -> x = genextreme.ppf(q^b, c=-xi, loc=mu, scale=sigma). JAWAB: 1) fit GEV. 2) per q: p = q^b. 3) ppf. 4) check vs empirical daily quantile at moderate q.
pitfalls: using q instead of q^b (gives a block quantile)

title: Constructing block maxima: calendar vs fixed-size blocks
deliverables: per-block table: block_start, block_end, n_obs, max_loss
frame: DIKETAHUI: dated returns [n]; block rule (calendar period or every b observations). DITANYAKAN: block maxima table [B]. RUMUS: losses L = -r; calendar: groupby(period).max(); fixed: reshape first floor(n/b) b obs into [B x b] and max over axis 1; incomplete trailing block dropped unless stated. JAWAB: 1) sort dates, drop NaN. 2) losses. 3) assign blocks. 4) max, date of max, n_obs per block. 5) apply minimum-count rule if given.
formulas: M_j = max_{i in block j} L_i
pitfalls: taking max of returns instead of max of losses

title: Gumbel fit to block maxima (xi fixed at 0)
deliverables: summary json: mu, sigma, return levels
frame: DIKETAHUI: block maxima [B]; return periods [P]. DITANYAKAN: Gumbel mu, sigma; return levels. RUMUS: H(x) = exp(-exp(-(x-mu)/sigma)); scipy gumbel_r.fit; MoM: sigma = s sqrt(6)/pi, mu = mean - 0.5772 sigma; z_m = mu - sigma ln(-ln(1-1/m)). JAWAB: 1) maxima. 2) fit (MLE or MoM as stated). 3) return levels. 4) optional LR test vs GEV: 2(LL_GEV - LL_Gumbel) ~ chi2_1.

title: GEV by probability-weighted moments / L-moments
frame: DIKETAHUI: block maxima [B]. DITANYAKAN: GEV parameters by PWM (Hosking-Wallis-Wood 1985). RUMUS: sort ascending; b0 = mean, b1 = (1/B) sum ((j-1)/(B-1)) x_(j), b2 = (1/B) sum ((j-1)(j-2)/((B-1)(B-2))) x_(j); l1 = b0, l2 = 2b1 - b0, t3 = (6b2 - 6b1 + b0)/l2; c = 2/(3+t3) - ln2/ln3; k = 7.8590 c + 2.9554 c^2; sigma = l2 k/((1 - 2^-k) Gamma(1+k)); mu = l1 + sigma(Gamma(1+k) - 1)/k; xi = -k. JAWAB: 1) b0..b2. 2) l-moments. 3) k, sigma, mu. 4) xi = -k.
pitfalls: Hosking k sign convention

title: GARCH-EVT one-day VaR and ES (McNeil-Frey)
deliverables: summary json: sigma_next, xi, beta, var_z, es_z, var, es
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns [n]; GARCH spec (mean, dist); threshold rule; levels [Q]. DITANYAKAN: sigma_{T+1}, residual-tail parameters, conditional VaR, ES. RUMUS: card Core 8: fit GARCH(1,1) (fit_garch11 or arch), z_t = (r_t - mu)/sigma_t, losses -z; POT on -z (own u); VaR_z, ES_z by Core 3; VaR = -mu + sigma_{T+1} VaR_z, ES = -mu + sigma_{T+1} ES_z. JAWAB: 1) GARCH fit (units!). 2) standardised residuals [n]. 3) POT on -z. 4) one-step sigma forecast. 5) scale. 6) check decimal units.
pitfalls: forgetting to rescale by sigma_{T+1}
percent vs decimal GARCH output

title: Rolling GARCH-EVT VaR backtest
deliverables: per-date table: date, var, loss, hit
summary json: n_hits, hit_rate, kupiec p-value
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns [n]; window W; refit frequency; level q. DITANYAKAN: one-step VaR series [n-W], hits, Kupiec test. RUMUS: card Core 8 each window: GARCH + POT on residuals -> VaR_{t+1}; hit_t = 1{L_t > VaR_t} (strict); kupiec_pof(hits, N, q); christoffersen_cc for independence. JAWAB: 1) loop t = W..n-1 using data up to t-1. 2) forecast VaR_t. 3) compare with realised loss. 4) count hits. 5) tests. 6) check no look-ahead.
pitfalls: using data through t to forecast t (look-ahead)

title: EVT vs normal vs historical VaR comparison table
deliverables: per-level x method table: level, method, var, es
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns [n]; levels [Q]; threshold rule. DITANYAKAN: VaR/ES per level and method. RUMUS: normal: var_es_normal(mu, sigma, q) (VaR = -mu + z sigma, ES = -mu + sigma phi(z)/(1-q)); historical: historical_var_es(returns, q) with pinned quantile rule; EVT: card Core 3. JAWAB: 1) losses. 2) moments (ddof stated). 3) three methods per q. 4) long table [Q x 3]. 5) check EVT > normal at extreme q for heavy tails.
pitfalls: quantile method mismatch across methods

title: ES to VaR ratio and tail asymptotics
deliverables: per-level table: level, var, es, ratio
frame: DIKETAHUI: GPD tail (u, xi, beta, N_u/n); levels [Q]. DITANYAKAN: ES_q/VaR_q per q and its limit. RUMUS: card Core 3 ES/VaR = 1/(1-xi) + (beta - xi u)/((1-xi) VaR_q) -> 1/(1-xi) as q -> 1 (xi > 0); xi=0 ratio -> 1; normal ratio -> 1. JAWAB: 1) VaR, ES per q. 2) ratio. 3) limit 1/(1-xi). 4) check ratio decreasing towards the limit.
pitfalls: infinite ES for xi >= 1

title: Multi-day EVT VaR by alpha-root scaling
frame: DIKETAHUI: 1-day EVT VaR_q; tail index alpha = 1/xi; horizon h. DITANYAKAN: h-day VaR by sqrt(h) and by h^(1/alpha). RUMUS: for sums of iid Pareto-tailed losses the far-tail quantile scales ~ h^(1/alpha) = h^xi (Danielsson-de Vries); normal scaling sqrt(h) (scale_horizon). JAWAB: 1) 1-day EVT VaR. 2) VaR_h = h^xi VaR_1. 3) compare sqrt(h). 4) state which rule the task asks; MC of h-day sums if path simulation is asked.
pitfalls: applying alpha-root scaling at moderate quantiles

title: Two-tailed EVT: separate GPD for losses and gains
deliverables: per-tail table: tail, u, n_exceed, xi, beta, var, es
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns [n]; threshold rule per tail; levels [Q]; position side. DITANYAKAN: GPD per tail; VaR/ES for long (losses = -r) and short (losses = +r). RUMUS: card Core 1-3 applied twice: lower tail on -r, upper tail on +r, each with its own u and N_u. JAWAB: 1) build both loss series. 2) thresholds. 3) two fits. 4) VaR, ES per side and level. 5) compare xi_left vs xi_right (asymmetry).
pitfalls: reusing the left-tail threshold for the right tail

title: EVT VaR in currency for a position value
deliverables: summary json: var_frac, es_frac, var_ccy, es_ccy
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns [n] (simple or log); position value V; level q. DITANYAKAN: VaR, ES in currency. RUMUS: card Core 3 in return units; simple returns: VaR_ccy = V x VaR_frac; log returns: loss = V(1 - exp(-VaR_log)) if conversion asked. JAWAB: 1) EVT on returns. 2) fraction VaR, ES. 3) multiply by V (or convert log). 4) report both units.
pitfalls: percent returns times V without /100

title: Semi-parametric tail: empirical body plus GPD tail CDF
frame: DIKETAHUI: losses [n]; threshold u; evaluation points x [M] or levels [Q]. DITANYAKAN: F(x) and F^-1(q). RUMUS: F(x) = empirical cdf for x <= u; F(x) = 1 - (N_u/n)(1 + xi(x-u)/beta)^(-1/xi) for x > u; inverse: empirical quantile if q <= 1 - N_u/n else Core 3 VaR_q. JAWAB: 1) fit tail. 2) evaluate piecewise. 3) check continuity at u (F(u) = 1 - N_u/n). 4) monotone.
pitfalls: discontinuity at u from >= vs > counting

title: Extremal index by the blocks method
deliverables: summary json: u, block_size, n_exceed, n_blocks_with_exceed, theta
frame: DIKETAHUI: losses [n]; threshold u; block length b. DITANYAKAN: extremal index theta (mean cluster size 1/theta). RUMUS: N = # exceedances, K = # blocks of length b with at least one exceedance, k = n/b blocks; theta = ln(1 - K/k)/(b ln(1 - N/n)) (or simple K/N). Clustered VaR: P(max over h days <= x) ~ F(x)^(h theta). JAWAB: 1) exceedance indicators. 2) blocks, K. 3) theta (stated estimator). 4) mean cluster size 1/theta.

title: Runs declustering before POT
deliverables: per-cluster table: start, end, size, cluster_max
frame: DIKETAHUI: dated losses [n]; threshold u; run length r. DITANYAKAN: clusters, cluster maxima, GPD on cluster peaks. RUMUS: a cluster ends after r consecutive non-exceedances; keep each cluster maximum; GPD MLE on peak excesses; tail rate uses n_c/n (Coles 2001 ch.5). JAWAB: 1) exceedance indicator. 2) scan with run rule -> cluster ids. 3) max per cluster. 4) fit. 5) theta ~ n_c/N_u. 6) VaR with clusters adjusted if asked.

title: Compound Poisson aggregate moments
deliverables: summary json: mean, variance, sd, skewness
frame: DIKETAHUI: Poisson rate lambda; severity distribution and parameters (currency). DITANYAKAN: E[S], Var[S], sd, skewness. RUMUS: card Core 9 E[S] = lambda E[X], Var[S] = lambda E[X^2], skew = lambda E[X^3]/(lambda E[X^2])^1.5; severity moments from card Completing (gamma, lognormal, Pareto); toolkit compound_poisson_moments(lam, m1, m2, m3). JAWAB: 1) raw moments of X. 2) aggregate moments. 3) check finite moments (Pareto alpha > 2, > 3).
pitfalls: using Var[X] instead of E[X^2]

title: Panjer recursion for compound Poisson
deliverables: per-node table: k, x, pmf, cdf
summary json: mean, var, var_q, es_q
frame: DIKETAHUI: lambda; severity pmf f [n] on grid h (or severity to discretise). DITANYAKAN: aggregate pmf g [n]; VaR/ES. RUMUS: card Core 10 g_0 = exp(-lambda(1-f_0)); g_s = (lambda/s) sum_{j=1..s} j f_j g_{s-j}; toolkit panjer_poisson(lam, f, n); aggregate_var_es(g, h, q). JAWAB: 1) discretise severity (Core 12). 2) recursion to n nodes. 3) cdf = cumsum. 4) check sum g ~ 1 and mean ~ lambda E[X]. 5) VaR, ES.
pitfalls: g_0 = exp(-lambda) when f_0 > 0

title: Panjer recursion for compound negative binomial
frame: DIKETAHUI: NB (r, beta) with mean r beta, var r beta(1+beta); severity pmf f [n]. DITANYAKAN: aggregate pmf g [n]. RUMUS: card Core 10 a = beta/(1+beta), b = (r-1)a; g_0 = PGF_N(f_0) = (1 + beta(1 - f_0))^(-r); g_s = (1/(1 - a f_0)) sum_{j=1..s} (a + b j/s) f_j g_{s-j}; toolkit panjer_negbin(r, beta, f, n) or panjer_ab. JAWAB: 1) map given NB parametrisation (n,p) -> (r, beta = (1-p)/p). 2) recursion. 3) check sum and mean r beta E[X].
formulas: g_s = sum (a + b j/s) f_j g_{s-j}/(1 - a f_0)
pitfalls: scipy nbinom (n,p) vs (r,beta) parametrisation

title: Panjer recursion for compound binomial
frame: DIKETAHUI: N ~ Bin(m, q); severity pmf f [n]. DITANYAKAN: aggregate pmf g. RUMUS: a = -q/(1-q), b = (m+1) q/(1-q); g_0 = (1 - q + q f_0)^m; Panjer (a,b,0) recursion; toolkit panjer_binomial(m, q, f, n). JAWAB: 1) discretised severity. 2) g_0. 3) recursion. 4) check mean m q E[X].

title: FFT aggregate loss for compound Poisson
frame: DIKETAHUI: lambda; severity (dist or pmf) ; h; n_grid. DITANYAKAN: aggregate pmf [n_grid], VaR/ES. RUMUS: card Core 11 g = real(ifft(exp(lambda(fft(f) - 1)))) on zero-padded f; clip negatives, renormalise; toolkit compound_poisson_fft(lam, f, n, pad=True), suggest_lattice for span. JAWAB: 1) choose h, n so n h > 99.99% quantile. 2) discretise (Core 12). 3) pad (x2 or next pow2). 4) FFT, PGF, iFFT. 5) truncate to n. 6) check sum 1, mean lambda E[X], g_0.
pitfalls: no padding / span too small (tail wraps)
forgetting real() and clipping

title: FFT aggregate loss with a general frequency PGF
frame: DIKETAHUI: frequency family and parameters; severity pmf f [n]. DITANYAKAN: aggregate pmf. RUMUS: g = real(ifft(PGF_N(fft(f)))); Poisson exp(lambda(z-1)); NB (1 - beta(z-1))^(-r); binomial (1 + q(z-1))^m; toolkit compound_fft(f, pgf, n, pad=True). JAWAB: 1) PGF as a function of complex z. 2) padded FFT. 3) apply PGF. 4) inverse, real, clip. 5) compare with Panjer for the same inputs.
pitfalls: complex power branch issues for non-integer r (use exp(-r log(...)))

title: Severity discretisation by rounding (mid-point)
frame: DIKETAHUI: severity dist and parameters; h; n. DITANYAKAN: f [n] on nodes k h. RUMUS: card Core 12 f_0 = F(h/2), f_k = F((k+1/2)h) - F((k-1/2)h); last node gets remaining mass 1 - F((n-1/2)h) or drop it (tail='drop'); toolkit severity_dist(name, ...), discretize_severity(dist, h, n, method='rounding'). JAWAB: 1) scipy dist (lognorm s, scale=e^mu; gamma a, scale). 2) cdf at half-nodes. 3) differences. 4) tail handling. 5) check sum, mean ~ E[X].
pitfalls: pdf(x) h instead of CDF differences

title: Lower and upper discretisation bounds
deliverables: per-method table: method, var, es, mean
frame: DIKETAHUI: severity; h; n; frequency. DITANYAKAN: aggregate VaR/ES under lower and upper discretisations (bracketing). RUMUS: lower (mass of [kh,(k+1)h) moved down to kh -> S stochastically smaller): f_k = F((k+1)h) - F(kh); upper (mass of ((k-1)h,kh] moved up to kh -> larger): f_0 = F(0), f_k = F(kh) - F((k-1)h); toolkit discretize_severity(method='lower'/'upper'). JAWAB: 1) both pmfs. 2) aggregate each (FFT/Panjer). 3) VaR/ES each. 4) check true value between and gap shrinking with h.
pitfalls: mislabeling which version is the upper bound

title: Mean-preserving local moment matching discretisation
deliverables: summary json: discretised mean, true mean
frame: DIKETAHUI: severity; h; n. DITANYAKAN: pmf preserving E[X] on each span. RUMUS: card Core 12 alternative (V5 c), Klugman-Panjer-Willmot one-moment matching: f_0 = 1 - E[X ^ h]/h; f_k = (2 E[X ^ kh] - E[X ^ (k-1)h] - E[X ^ (k+1)h])/h, using limited expected value E[X ^ d] = int_0^d S(x) dx. JAWAB: 1) LEV function (closed form or quad). 2) f_0, f_k. 3) check sum 1 and sum k h f_k = E[X] (up to truncation).
pitfalls: confusing limited expected value with raw moment

title: Aggregate VaR and ES from a lattice pmf
frame: DIKETAHUI: pmf g [n] on grid h; levels [Q]. DITANYAKAN: VaR, ES in currency. RUMUS: card Conventions: VaR_a = h x first k with cumsum(g) >= a; ES Acerbi-Tasche = (1/(1-a))[sum_{x>VaR} x g + VaR (F(VaR) - a)] (V4 b); strict E[S|S>VaR] when text writes '>' (V4 a); toolkit aggregate_var_es(g, h, level, es_mode). JAWAB: 1) cdf. 2) VaR index. 3) ES per stated variant. 4) x = index x h. 5) check ES >= VaR.
pitfalls: mixing strict and Acerbi-Tasche ES

title: Monte Carlo aggregate loss and comparison with FFT
deliverables: summary json: mc_var, mc_es, fft_var, fft_es, rel_diff
frame: DIKETAHUI: lambda; severity; n_sims; seed; levels. DITANYAKAN: MC VaR/ES, FFT VaR/ES, relative differences. RUMUS: card Conventions MC: rng = default_rng(seed); N = rng.poisson(lambda, n_sims); X = sev.rvs(sum N, random_state=rng); S = bincount(repeat(arange, N), X); sample VaR sorted[ceil(a n)-1]; toolkit compound_poisson_mc. JAWAB: 1) simulate counts then severities in one call. 2) aggregate. 3) VaR, ES. 4) FFT on lattice. 5) relative differences.
pitfalls: drawing severities per scenario in a loop (different stream order than pinned)

title: Choosing lattice span and step to avoid FFT aliasing
deliverables: summary json: h, n, span, tail_mass_beyond_span
frame: DIKETAHUI: lambda; severity; target level. DITANYAKAN: h, n_grid; check of truncated mass. RUMUS: span n h > aggregate 99.99% quantile (card Conventions: ~2x max(MC 99.99% quantile, mean + 10 sd)); n power of 2; h small relative to severity scale; toolkit suggest_lattice(lam, dist, level). JAWAB: 1) moments -> mean + 10 sd. 2) optional quick MC quantile. 3) span, n, h. 4) after FFT: check mass in last nodes ~ 0 and pmf at 0 equals exp(-lambda(1-f_0)).
formulas: span = n h >= 2 max(q_99.99, mean + 10 sd)
pitfalls: heavy-tailed severity needs much wider span

title: Pareto and Lomax severity conventions
deliverables: summary json: mean, second moment, simulated mean
frame: DIKETAHUI: Pareto alpha, x_m (or Lomax alpha, theta); n_sims. DITANYAKAN: moments, samples, cdf for discretisation. RUMUS: card Conventions classical Pareto S(x) = (x_m/x)^alpha, x >= x_m: scipy pareto(b=alpha, scale=x_m); numpy rng.pareto(a) is Lomax: classical = (rng.pareto(a)+1) x_m; Lomax S(x) = (theta/(x+theta))^alpha: scipy lomax(c=alpha, scale=theta). Mean alpha x_m/(alpha-1); E[X^2] alpha x_m^2/(alpha-2). JAWAB: 1) identify parametrisation. 2) moments with existence checks. 3) sample or discretise.
pitfalls: treating rng.pareto output as classical Pareto

title: Calibrating lognormal severity from mean and CV
deliverables: summary json: mu, sigma, check mean, check sd
frame: DIKETAHUI: severity mean m and sd s (or CV, or median and a quantile). DITANYAKAN: lognormal mu, sigma; scipy parameters. RUMUS: sigma^2 = ln(1 + (s/m)^2), mu = ln m - sigma^2/2; from median M and q-quantile x_q: mu = ln M, sigma = (ln x_q - mu)/z_q; scipy lognorm(s=sigma, scale=exp(mu)). JAWAB: 1) solve. 2) build dist. 3) verify mean, sd. 4) continue to aggregate.
pitfalls: passing mu as scipy scale

title: Operational risk LDA capital at 99.9%
deliverables: summary json: el, var_999, ul, capital
frame: DIKETAHUI: annual frequency lambda (or NB); severity fit; level a (99.9%). DITANYAKAN: EL, VaR_a, UL = VaR - EL, capital (VaR or UL as stated). RUMUS: aggregate by FFT/Panjer/MC (card Core 9-12); EL = lambda E[X]; VaR_a from lattice; capital = VaR (or VaR - EL if EL is provisioned). JAWAB: 1) severity params. 2) lattice. 3) aggregate pmf. 4) VaR, EL, UL. 5) sum across cells if independent (or by convolution).
pitfalls: summing cell VaRs vs VaR of convolution (diversification)

title: Aggregate loss with per-loss deductible and limit
deliverables: summary json: lambda_paid, mean_payment, aggregate mean, var_q
frame: DIKETAHUI: lambda; ground-up severity X; deductible d; limit l (layer l xs d). DITANYAKAN: payment-per-loss or per-payment distribution; aggregate. RUMUS: per-loss Y_L = min(max(X - d, 0), l); per-payment: frequency thinned lambda' = lambda S(d), severity X - d | X > d capped at l; E[Y_L] = E[X ^ (d+l)] - E[X ^ d]. JAWAB: 1) choose per-payment form. 2) thinned frequency. 3) discretise conditional severity (with atom at l). 4) aggregate. 5) check mean = lambda E[Y_L].
pitfalls: forgetting the probability atom at the limit

title: Stop-loss premium from the aggregate distribution
frame: DIKETAHUI: aggregate pmf g on grid h; retentions d [D]. DITANYAKAN: E[(S - d)+] per d. RUMUS: E[(S-d)+] = sum_k max(kh - d, 0) g_k; recursion on grid d_j = jh: SL(d_{j+1}) = SL(d_j) - h (1 - F(d_j)); SL(0) = E[S]. JAWAB: 1) aggregate pmf. 2) per d sum, or recursion. 3) check SL(0) = E[S], decreasing convex in d.

title: Single-loss approximation for subexponential severity
frame: DIKETAHUI: lambda; heavy-tailed severity F; level a. DITANYAKAN: SLA VaR and comparison. RUMUS: VaR_a ~ F^-1(1 - (1-a)/lambda) (Bocker-Kluppelberg 2005); mean-corrected: + (lambda - 1) E[X] (finite mean). JAWAB: 1) p = 1 - (1-a)/lambda. 2) severity ppf. 3) optional correction. 4) compare with FFT/MC VaR.
pitfalls: using it for light-tailed severity

title: Spliced severity: empirical or lognormal body with GPD tail
deliverables: summary json: u, p_tail, xi, beta
frame: DIKETAHUI: individual losses [m]; threshold u; frequency lambda. DITANYAKAN: spliced severity cdf, discretised pmf, aggregate VaR. RUMUS: F(x) = (1 - p) F_body(x)/F_body(u) for x <= u; F(x) = 1 - p (1 + xi(x-u)/beta)^(-1/xi) for x > u, p = N_u/m. JAWAB: 1) fit body (empirical or truncated parametric). 2) GPD on excesses. 3) spliced cdf. 4) discretise by CDF differences. 5) aggregate. 6) VaR/ES.
pitfalls: body not renormalised to mass 1 - p

title: Aggregating independent business lines by convolution
deliverables: summary json: total var, sum of var, diversification
frame: DIKETAHUI: per line: lambda_i, severity_i; common h, n. DITANYAKAN: per-line VaR, total VaR, diversification benefit. RUMUS: independent compound Poisson sum = compound Poisson with lambda = sum lambda_i and mixed severity f = sum (lambda_i/lambda) f_i; or g_total = ifft(prod fft(g_i)) on padded grid. JAWAB: 1) common lattice. 2) per-line aggregate. 3) total via product of transforms. 4) VaR per line and total. 5) benefit = sum VaR_i - VaR_total.
pitfalls: different h per line

title: Fitting frequency: Poisson vs negative binomial
deliverables: summary json: mean, var, lambda, r, beta, chosen
frame: DIKETAHUI: loss counts per period [P]. DITANYAKAN: Poisson lambda; NB (r, beta) if overdispersed; choice. RUMUS: Poisson MLE lambda = mean; dispersion var/mean; NB by moments beta = var/mean - 1, r = mean/beta (var > mean); NB MLE optional; AIC comparison. JAWAB: 1) mean, var (ddof stated). 2) lambda. 3) NB moments. 4) LL of both, AIC. 5) choose.
pitfalls: NB moment fit when var <= mean

title: GPD goodness of fit: QQ, KS and Anderson-Darling
frame: DIKETAHUI: excesses [N_u]; fitted xi, beta. DITANYAKAN: QQ coordinates, KS statistic and p-value. RUMUS: plotting positions p_i = i/(N+1); model quantiles genpareto.ppf(p_i, xi, 0, beta); KS: scipy kstest(y, 'genpareto', args=(xi, 0, beta)) (p-value optimistic when parameters estimated; parametric bootstrap if asked). JAWAB: 1) sort excesses. 2) QQ pairs. 3) KS / AD. 4) interpret.
pitfalls: KS p-value without bootstrap after fitting

title: Bootstrap confidence interval for EVT VaR
deliverables: summary json: var_hat, ci_lower, ci_upper, n_boot
frame: DIKETAHUI: losses [n]; threshold rule; level q; B replications; seed. DITANYAKAN: VaR_q and bootstrap percentile CI. RUMUS: resample losses with replacement (or excesses), refit u and GPD each time, VaR_q^(b) by Core 3; CI = quantiles (alpha/2, 1-alpha/2) of VaR^(b). JAWAB: 1) rng = default_rng(seed). 2) B loops. 3) VaR per replicate. 4) percentile CI. 5) check CI contains point estimate.
pitfalls: keeping the threshold fixed when the task says recompute

title: Empirical tail VaR and ES on a sample (quantile conventions)
frame: DIKETAHUI: losses [n]; levels [Q]; quantile rule. DITANYAKAN: empirical VaR, ES (benchmark for EVT). RUMUS: card V6 a VaR = sorted_asc[ceil(a n) - 1] (np.quantile method='inverted_cdf'); b: np.quantile linear; ES = mean(L | L >= VaR) or > VaR as text states; toolkit historical_var_es(returns, level, method). JAWAB: 1) losses. 2) sort. 3) VaR per stated rule. 4) ES. 5) compare EVT VaR near threshold level.
pitfalls: percentile (0-100) vs quantile (0-1) argument

title: Tail index from log-log rank regression (Zipf plot)
frame: DIKETAHUI: losses [n]; k largest. DITANYAKAN: alpha from slope of log rank vs log size. RUMUS: for i = 1..k: ln(i/n) ~ c - alpha ln X_(i); OLS slope = -alpha; Gabaix-Ibragimov correction uses ln(i - 1/2). JAWAB: 1) sort descending. 2) y = ln(i - 0.5) (or ln i), x = ln X_(i). 3) OLS. 4) alpha = -slope, xi = 1/alpha. 5) compare to Hill.
pitfalls: OLS se understated (use alpha sqrt(2/k))

title: EVT tail fit on a weighted portfolio return series
deliverables: summary json: weights, u, xi, beta, var, es
frame: DIKETAHUI: prices [T x N]; weights [N]; threshold rule; levels. DITANYAKAN: portfolio loss tail and VaR/ES. RUMUS: r_t = prices pct_change (or log) per stated kind; r_p = r w (toolkit portfolio_returns); L = -r_p; card Core 1-3. JAWAB: 1) sort dates, drop NaN jointly. 2) asset returns [T-1 x N]. 3) portfolio [T-1]. 4) POT fit. 5) VaR/ES; currency if value given.
pitfalls: using log returns with linear weights without stating approximation

title: Hill estimator on the upper tail of absolute returns
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns [n]; k. DITANYAKAN: tail indices for losses, gains, |r|; which moments exist. RUMUS: card Core 6 on X = -r, X = r, X = |r|; moment of order p finite iff p < alpha (variance needs alpha > 2, kurtosis alpha > 4). JAWAB: 1) three series. 2) Hill at k each. 3) alpha. 4) moment existence statements.

title: Return period of a historical loss under GEV
frame: DIKETAHUI: annual maxima fit (mu, sigma, xi); a loss level x. DITANYAKAN: P(annual max > x), return period. RUMUS: p = 1 - H(x) = 1 - exp(-(1 + xi (x-mu)/sigma)^(-1/xi)); return period = 1/p blocks; scipy genextreme.sf(x, c=-xi, loc, scale). JAWAB: 1) fit. 2) sf. 3) 1/p. 4) note if x beyond upper endpoint (xi < 0: mu - sigma/xi) -> p = 0.
